title: Improve streaming header propagation and scoped signature semantics for OpenAI-compat layer
author: Amelia Chen
description:
Context: Streaming endpoints (SSE/WebSocket/progressive HTTP) need predictable auth semantics across preflight, initial handshake, and per-chunk delivery. Tool/function-calling and structured-output features rely on stable header propagation so downstream runtime routing and function authorization can reason about the request principal and scope. Previous inconsistencies caused 1) dropped project-scoped keys on CORS preflight + SSE upgrade, and 2) inability to validate per-chunk integrity for long-lived streams when using short-lived scoped tokens.

This PR unifies header handling across: the OpenAI-compat translation layer, streaming proxy, and the runtime auth middlewares. It introduces a backwards-compatible signed-chunk header and clarifies semantics for project/org-scoped tokens and nonce exchange.

What this PR changes (high level):
- Adds X-Redwood-Project and X-Redwood-Scope canonical propagation headers emitted by the compat layer when translating Authorization Bearer -> internal credential routing.
- Implements X-Redwood-Session-Nonce exchange header for browser flows. The server returns a short-lived nonce on successful preflight/handshake so clients can sign subsequent chunk frames.
- Adds chunk integrity header X-Redwood-Chunk-Sig (HMAC-SHA256 over chunk payload + sequence id) and validation in the streaming proxy. This supports long-lived SSE/WS streams without requiring reauth per message.
- Extends CORS preflight handling to explicitly allow Signed-Session and Chunk-Sig headers and exposes the Session-Nonce on responses. Policy: Access-Control-Allow-Headers includes Signed-Session, X-Redwood-Chunk-Sig, X-Redwood-Session-Nonce; Access-Control-Expose-Headers exposes X-Redwood-Session-Nonce.
- OpenAI-compat layer: when an Authorization: Bearer <token> is received, we attempt to resolve scope -> emit X-Redwood-Project & X-Redwood-Scope and a short-lived internal credential header (X-Redwood-Internal-Cred). Legacy clients without compatibility will continue to work (compat translations are opt-out via a header).
- Adds integration tests for SSE and WebSocket handshake flows, plus unit tests for signature verification edge cases (replay, out-of-order seq ids).

Notes on rollout and safety:
- Backwards compatible by default: clients that don't send Signed-Session or Chunk-Sig continue to function; only streams opt into stricter chunk validation when the server issues a Session-Nonce.
- Feature gate: compat_layer.header_translation can be toggled per-route (console + config flag) to assist staged migration and canary.
- Canary plan: enable for 5% of streaming traffic in prod for 48 hours, monitor error_rate/latency and chunk_signature_failures metric.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed by security and runtime teams
- [x] Unit tests for signature verification and header translation
- [x] Integration tests for SSE/WS preflight and handshake
- [x] OpenAI-compat translation implemented and feature-gated
- [x] SDK updates (JS + Python) with minimal client helpers (signChunk helper)
- [x] Docs updated (auth headers and CORS notes)

Risk: medium. Primary risk is accidental exposure of internal credential header; mitigated via strict translation rules, per-route feature gate, and scrub/strip logic at the public ingress layer.

Follow-ups (future PRs):
- Add support for asymmetric signing (Ed25519) for cross-service verification (ENG-9902).
- Add server-side rotation hints for Session-Nonce lifetimes (ENG-10010).

release_notes: Auth: add canonical X-Redwood-Project and X-Redwood-Scope headers emitted by the OpenAI-compat layer when possible.
Security: support per-chunk HMAC signatures (X-Redwood-Chunk-Sig) and Session-Nonce exchange for long-lived streams.
CORS: explicit preflight allowlist for signed-session headers and expose Session-Nonce to browser clients.
Compatibility: opt-out header X-Redwood-Compat: none to disable automatic header translation.
summary: Add canonical project/scope headers, Session-Nonce exchange, and per-chunk signatures to make streaming stable and secure while keeping OpenAI-compat behavior configurable and back-compatible.
